ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$4.47 (3.17 km × S$1.41/km) as a Ryde voucher for the un-exempted off-route segment; note in the file that the Sims Avenue detour was not consented to before departure (driver asked, rider agreed, but the agreed route was itself the deviating route) and remind the driver to keep to the shortest and most direct route absent a reasonable cause verified by traffic data.

segment_findings.reason: The 12:27–12:36 off-route segment (+3.17 km, up to 1174 m from optimal) is not exempt: the only 'agreement' is the rider assenting to the driver's own proposed Sims Avenue route [F7][F8], which is not a rider-issued routing instruction under RD-3(a) and does not satisfy RD-5's requirement of a mutual agreement to change route before departure; the driver's post-trip statement of verbal agreement cannot supply consent (G11), and no RD-4 reasonable cause exists — PIE/CTE are only band 4 [F11][F12] and no incident was recorded [F13].

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally is a claim, not consent; RD-5 requires the rider's own message sent before the detour began (G11).
PIE speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) is outside bands 1–2 and, per RD-4(b), a band record cannot exempt a segment on its own; it also does not evidence the alternative route's congestion.
CTE band 4 likewise fails RD-4(b) and was not shown to be on the replaced optimal-route stretch.
